answer.reason: The verses tell of Caleb's stand as a spy, his sparing from the wilderness judgment, and his inheritance of Hebron.

clauses.english: urged Israel to go up at once and possess the land, when the other spies brought back an evil report
clauses.quote: Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.

clauses.english: was spared, with Joshua, when the LORD doomed the rest of that generation to die in the wilderness
clauses.quote: But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land

clauses.english: received Hebron as his inheritance and drove out the three sons of Anak
clauses.quote: And Caleb drove thence the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai

doubts: JOS 14:7 and JOS 14:10 give Caleb's ages (forty and eighty-five) rather than a birth or death, so the dataset's birth and death events were not used.
Othniel's winning of Achsah and his judging of Israel (JOS 15:17, JDG 3:9) are deeds of Othniel, not Caleb, so they were left out.
